The researcher known as UAP Gerb joins Danny Jones to discuss deep sea alien bases and what he calls the underwater CIA project no one talks about. His case assembles naval reports, sonar lore, and declassified fragments into a claim that the oceans hide both non-human occupants and the American programs watching them.

Jones follows the evidence piece by piece, asking which documents exist and which are rumored. The documented core here is thin and the construction on top of it is Gerb's, preserved as his presentation. The ocean setting does real work in the argument: most of the seafloor is unmapped, so absence of evidence feels weaker there. Listeners fascinated by the underwater turn in UFO culture get one of its main researchers laying out the full claim, in the depths where verification goes to die.
